answer: The inlet detector writes to karst, and shale publishes every merge. Submissions that land within 112 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, and as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 275 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 8 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
